- Whether Redwood requires a watermark on content distributed externally.

Hi Sophie —

Thanks for the timestamp sheet. Quick answers and a few questions from our side:

- Slate: 3s static slate is fine. Preferred deliverable: 1920x1080 PNG (RGB) and a 1920x1080 .mov of the slate for stitching (we have a template for safe title margins). Please keep the sponsor logo centered on the right third — avoid full-bleed backgrounds.
- Watermark: Redwood policy is to avoid persistent watermarks on partner-owned content. If BrightBridge insists on an overlay, it must be non-obtrusive and removed on request. We need sponsor acknowledgement to accept any watermarking requests.
- Rights: we need a signed sponsor asset release confirming non-exclusive distribution; legal prefers a 3-year window by default, perpetual requires written approval. Marissa — can you confirm we have precedence for perpetual grant?
- Captions: provide separate SRTs; we will not burn captions by default (preserves flexibility). We can burn-in on request but that is an extra transcode step.

Technical: our encoding pipeline accepts H.264 baseline/main for web; MP4 container preferred. Max deliverable bitrate for 1080p: 6 Mbps constant or variable up to 10 Mbps if you provide originals. Please also provide a high-bitrate master (final_master_recording.mp4) if possible — that speeds up clipping and quality checks.

One more ask: include a separate folder for sponsor-approved thumbnails and a short sponsor legal contact email (for the release). Once we have signed release and final assets, we can start stitching and push proofs the same day.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Platform Ops Manager, Redwood Inference

Quick ops note — tagging with encoder constraints and timeline:

- We can stitch slates server-side before transcoding; please provide slate.mov (3s) and the PNG. If you only provide PNG we'll create the slate.mov but it introduces a small color-match risk.
- Caption workflow: if you supply SRTs, we'll mux them into the MP4 and include separate VTT for web. If you request burned-in captions, add +1 business day to turnaround.
- Watermark removal: if sponsor requires watermark, we can place watermark layer for their pre-approved promos, but internal policy requires that any Redwood-origin clips (e.g., those we re-host) must not have third-party sponsor watermarks. We'll mark clips as "sponsor-owned" in metadata so routing/hosting rules respect that.

Schedule proposal:
- 2027-06-22: receive signed asset release + assets and slate
- 2027-06-23: ingest and first-pass stitching / QC proofs (watermark/burn-in options applied per request)
- 2027-06-24: review with BrightBridge (proofs)
- 2027-06-27: final delivery to client + distribution pack (thumbnails, SRTs, master references)

Ben Carter
Streaming Ops Lead, Redwood Inference
